title: Job 32
paragraphs: ¹ So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. ² But Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger. He was furious with Job for justifying himself rather than God, ³ and angry with the three friends for failing to find an answer and yet condemning Job anyway. ⁴ Elihu had held back from speaking while they talked, because they were older than he. ⁵ But when he saw that the three had nothing more to say, his anger flared.

⁶ So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite said, "I am young, and you are very old; that is why I held back from telling you what I know. ⁷ I thought, 'Let age speak; let many years teach wisdom.' ⁸ But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding. ⁹ The wise are not always old, nor do elders always understand what is just. ¹⁰ Therefore I say: Listen to me. I too will tell you what I know.

¹¹ I waited while you searched for the right words; I gave ear while you reasoned things through. ¹² I listened carefully — but not one of you proved Job wrong or answered what he said. ¹³ Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God refute him, not man.' ¹⁴ Job has not directed his words at me, and I will not answer him with your arguments. ¹⁵ They are dismayed; they have no more to say — words have left them entirely.

¹⁶ I have waited — and since they stand there in silence with nothing more to say, ¹⁷ I too will have my turn. I will say what I know. ¹⁸ For I am full of words; the spirit inside me compels me. ¹⁹ Inside I am like bottled wine with no outlet, like new wineskins about to burst. ²⁰ I must speak and find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
²¹ I will show no partiality to anyone; I will flatter no one. ²² For I do not know how to flatter — if I did, my Maker would soon take me away.
